title: The strip's 98 per-day countEvents calls are two thirds of a Ledger render
body:
## Summary
readStrip calls countEvents once per strip day (84 past days) and each call runs 16 statements (total, head, and 7 facets x 2), all to read one facet (actorKind); it re-runs on every live refresh.

## Description
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:233-253 loops the strip's days and calls countEvents (packages/kernel/src/events-count.ts:66-99), which computes the total, the head and all seven facets with two statements each. The strip uses only the actorKind split. 84 calls x 16 = 1,344 SQL statements per render, synchronous on the server, repeated on every coalesced router.refresh() from the live feed. What fixed looks like: one kernel read that groups by UTC day and actor kind over the window under the filter (a GROUP BY substr(t,1,10), actor_kind), or a countEvents option naming the facets wanted. The kernel is another context (packages/kernel), so this round could not build it.

## Flow
- open /ledger on a store of 100k events
- page.tsx readView -> readPage + readFacets + readStrip
- readStrip runs 84 countEvents -> 517 ms of a 687 ms read
- every live arrival burst repeats it via router.refresh()

## Expected impact
Every Ledger render and live refresh on a large store gets ~3/4 of its read time back; measured by the probe below. A kernel per-day read must keep the half-open day windows exact or the strip and the click-through list disagree.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one render's read time
Before: probe (in-memory kernel, 3 actor kinds, 84 days): N=20k readPage 11 ms, readFacets 40 ms, readStrip 137 ms; N=100k readPage 10 ms, readFacets 160 ms, readStrip 517 ms
After: not taken - needs a kernel per-day count API (out of scope)
Method: probe - scratch script over the real read.ts and an in-memory kernel, 5 reps, median; the After needs a kernel change this round does not own
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:233-253 (for day of days -> countEvents)
packages/kernel/src/events-count.ts:73-92 (GROUPS.map: 2 statements per facet)
probe N=100000: readStrip median 517.1 ms vs readPage 9.9 ms, readFacets 159.9 ms
instrument: the strip probe (in-memory kernel, N=20k/100k, median of 5 readStrip calls) plus ledger-read.test.ts readStrip cases unchanged green; out-of-scope seam: packages/kernel events-count

title: An earlier burst's flash timer clears a later burst's flash early
body:
## Summary
Ledger.tsx schedules a FRESH_MS clear per coalesced burst and never cancels the previous one, so a second burst's arrivals stop flashing when the FIRST burst's timer fires; the timers also outlive unmount.

## Description
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Ledger.tsx (live block, onEvents): burst A at t=0 refreshes at 700 ms and sets a clear at 2000 ms; burst B at 1000 ms refreshes at 1700 ms and setFresh(B) - then A's clear at 2000 ms empties it after 300 ms instead of 1300. The unmount cleanup clears only the coalesce timer. Fixed: one clear timer held in a ref, replaced per burst and cleared on unmount.

## Flow
- two act bursts land 1 s apart (a sync appending in two chunks)
- the second burst's rows flash ~300 ms, not 1300 ms

## Expected impact
The operator sees each arrival flash for its full beat; tiny visual change, no data risk.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an arrival's flash lasts FRESH_MS
Before: walked: burst B flashes 300 ms of 1300
After: predicted: 1300 ms
Method: simulation - the client hook has no DOM test lane here; a fake-timer test needs the coalescer extracted
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Ledger.tsx onEvents: window.setTimeout(() => setFresh(new Set()), FRESH_MS) with no handle kept; cleanup clears timer.current only
instrument: extract the coalescer as a pure function over injected timers and drive it with vitest fake timers: B's set must survive until B+FRESH_MS

title: Five clipboard sites call navigator.clipboard unguarded
body:
## Summary
Ledger.tsx and four audio-route sites call navigator.clipboard.writeText directly; outside a secure context navigator.clipboard is undefined and the call throws synchronously, past the .then rejection handler, so the toast never comes.

## Description
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Ledger.tsx (copy), app/(studio)/audio/_audio/Arrange.tsx:303, app/(studio)/audio/_audio/AudioLane.tsx:122, app/(studio)/audio/_hunt/Hunt.tsx:197 (and the dev inspector guards it with `navigator.clipboard?.writeText`). Five hand-rolled spellings of one act, one of them guarded. Fixed: one shared copy helper (in @gt/ui or the shell) that answers a refusal for an absent clipboard, adopted at every site.

## Flow
- open the studio over plain http on a LAN address
- press Copy JSONL / copy on the Ledger
- TypeError thrown in the click handler, nothing said

## Expected impact
A copy outside localhost/https says why it refused instead of doing nothing. Touches the audio route (another context).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - duplicated sites behind one helper
Before: 5 sites, 1 guarded (dev inspector)
After: predicted: 1 helper, 5 of 5 sites guarded
Method: probe - sites counted by grep; not built: 4 of 5 sites are outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn 'clipboard' app packages/ui/src: Ledger.tsx:178, Arrange.tsx:303, AudioLane.tsx:122, Hunt.tsx:197 unguarded; DevInspector.tsx:37 guarded
instrument: a vitest case calling the helper with navigator.clipboard undefined: it must resolve to a refusal, not throw; plus a grep ratchet for bare navigator.clipboard.writeText under app/

title: The older action's 4000-char search cap is narrower than what the page renders
body:
## Summary
page.tsx renders any q the URL carries, but olderEvents' door caps the page's search string at 4000 chars, so a long-query Ledger draws page 1 and then refuses every 'older' with an invalid-input toast.

## Description
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/actions.ts:9 (`search: z.string().max(4000)`) vs filter.ts parseParams, which trims q but bounds neither its length nor the comma lists. MAX_WORDS caps free words at 8, not characters; a token value or a pasted id list can carry the search past 4000 encoded chars (encodeURIComponent triples non-ASCII). Fixed: bound q (and lists) in parseParams to what the door accepts, so page and action read the same filter - a policy choice on the cap, hence not built unattended.

## Flow
- open /ledger?q=<a 4001-char query>
- page 1 renders
- press older -> 'ledger older: invalid' toast, every time

## Expected impact
A long filter either pages or is visibly trimmed; nobody meets a Ledger whose 'older' can never work.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one filter, one length rule
Before: walked: q of 4001 chars renders, older refuses
After: predicted: parseParams trims to the door's bound; older pages
Method: simulation - the door and the parser read side by side; a test is S but the cap value is a call
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/actions.ts: search: z.string().max(4000)
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/filter.ts parseParams: q: one(p, "q").trim() (no length bound)
instrument: vitest: parseParams of a 5000-char q, then olderInput.safeParse({search: toSearch(f), cursor}) must succeed

title: The live feed drops a malformed event or reset frame without a word
body:
## Summary
feed.ts parses each event frame's seq and each reset frame's head through the door and silently skips a refusal: no console line, no count, the cursor not advanced.

## Description
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/feed.ts: `if (e.ok) { ... }` for event frames and `if (r.ok) cursor = ...` for reset frames - 2 of 2 parse-failure paths swallowed, while the transport failure path does console.error. A server that changed its frame shape would leave the page live-looking (heartbeats keep the edge green) and never refreshing. Fixed: a console.error naming the frame and the door's message on each refusal (policy-tighten: logs more).

## Flow
- server sends `data: {"sequence":5}` (a renamed field)
- parseJsonAt refuses
- nothing logged; the page never refreshes; the badge says live

## Expected impact
A wire drift shows in the console the first time it happens. Logging more is policy-tighten.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - swallowed errors on the feed
Before: 2 of 2 frame-parse refusals swallowed
After: predicted: 0 of 2
Method: probe - sites counted by reading; the hook needs a DOM/fetch-stub test lane this repo's vitest (node) does not have for client hooks
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/feed.ts event branch: const e = parseJsonAt(...); if (e.ok) {...}
reset branch: if (r.ok) cursor = r.value.head;
instrument: a vitest case driving useLedgerFeed's frame loop extracted as a pure reducer (frames -> {seqs, cursor, logs}); a malformed frame must yield one log line

title: Live arrivals never reach an oldest-first Ledger read to its end
body:
## Summary
Under order=asc the first page is the oldest 500 and never changes on refresh; once 'older' (newer, in asc) has read to the end, the tail has no cursor and arrivals are neither drawn nor reachable.

## Description
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Ledger.tsx rows = rowsOf(p.page.events, more): a refresh redraws p.page (still the oldest 500) and `more` is the client's stale copy; `tail.exhausted` hides the older button (List.tsx `p.capped`). The live arrivals flash set names seqs no drawn row holds. Fixed: in asc with an exhausted tail, a refresh re-reads past the last drawn row (the cursor of the last row) through the older action, or the live handler does.

## Flow
- /ledger?order=asc on a ledger under 1000 acts
- press older until it disappears
- an act lands: the total ticks, no row appears, no button to fetch it

## Expected impact
Oldest-first readers see new acts arrive; today they must reload.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an arrival is drawn in both orders
Before: walked: asc + exhausted tail -> 0 of N arrivals drawn
After: predicted: N of N
Method: simulation - needs the client hook's refresh path exercised; no DOM lane
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: Ledger.tsx: rows = rowsOf(p.page.events, more); tail = more?.page ?? p.page; List.tsx: {p.capped && <older button>}
instrument: a pure 'rows after refresh' reducer over (order, first page, older state, arrived seqs) tested in ledger-filter.test.ts: asc + exhausted + arrivals must yield a fetch of the cursor past the last drawn row

title: Below ~670 px the column head and the rows scroll apart
body:
## Summary
The table's column grid is fixed (--ledger-cols sums to ~566 px plus gaps and padding, ~670 px) and the column head sits outside the scroll container, so at phone width the rows scroll horizontally under a head that does not.

## Description
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/ledger.module.css `.cols` (outside `.scroll`) and List.tsx (the head is a sibling of the scroller); tokens: --ledger-cols: 54px 96px 128px 128px minmax(0,1fr) 70px 90px. The drawers at 1360/1280 px handle the rail and detail; nothing handles the table itself under its own minimum. Whether the studio targets phones is the operator's call; the defect is the misalignment wherever the viewport is under the minimum.

## Flow
- open /ledger at 390 px
- scroll the rows sideways
- the head stays put; columns no longer line up with their names

## Expected impact
A narrow window reads its own columns. Measured by a capture at 390 px.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - head aligned with rows at a named width
Before: computed: table minimum ~670 px > 390 px; head outside the scroller
After: not taken
Method: simulation - a reproduced viewport needs a dev server (cx-capture), which a round-agent may not run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/ui tokens: --ledger-cols: 54px 96px 128px 128px minmax(0,1fr) 70px 90px
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/List.tsx: <div className={s.cols}> is a sibling of <div ref={scroller} className={s.scroll}>
instrument: CX_BASE=... node pipeline/cx-capture.mjs ledger out.png --width 390 before and after; or a live probe reading the head's and first row's column x offsets after a horizontal scroll

title: Reading the Ledger is not itself recorded
body:
## Summary
audit-logging: audit-querying says reading a sensitive trail is an auditable act and the reader set is a decision; the Ledger's reads (page, older, related, /api/ledger, MCP read) record nothing.

## Description
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/actions.ts runs principal("read") and writes no event; page.tsx likewise. The technique calls 'whoever can open the app' defensible for a single-operator tool - which this is - so this is a direction call, not a defect: whether agent reads (MCP, /api/ledger) should land a read-access record in the ledger.

## Flow
- an agent reads /api/ledger?format=jsonl
- no record that it read anything

## Expected impact
Answers 'who has been reading the history' for agent reads. Adds write volume per read.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - audit completeness for reads
Before: 0 of 5 read doors record a read
After: a direction decision
Method: simulation - the technique read against the doors; the benefit is a policy question
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: ai-registry audit-logging/techniques/audit-querying.md 'Reading the trail is itself an auditable act'; actions.ts olderEvents/relatedEvents: principal("read") then read only
